portfolio.title: Web Portfolio
portfolio.description_short: This is the website you are visiting right now! My personal, self-developed web portfolio. Here I applied all my knowledge of React and Next.js to create this page as an online CV to showcase my projects. My entire professional background is summarized here, so if you want to know more about me, just keep exploring!
portfolio.description_long: This is the website you are visiting right now! My personal, self-developed web portfolio. Here I applied all my knowledge of React and Next.js to create this page as an online CV to showcase my projects, experiences, and entire professional career. The web app is deployed on www.vercel.com, an online hosting service that uses AWS. I develop the website locally using React, Next.js, Tailwind, custom hooks, components, etc., and via GitHub Actions it is automatically deployed on Vercel.

procedural.title: Procedural Animations
procedural.description_short: In this project, I employed the concept of zero keyframes: instead of using images for texture, I drew and rendered the frames of a moving creature to make it appear alive. The main idea was to create fish-like creatures with fins and wobbly eyes. I then incorporated some of my previous work on Inverse Kinematics to generate the legs. The results are incredible visuals of creatures that move as if they were alive!
procedural.description_long: Using Python, Pygame, and NumPy, I employed the concept of zero keyframes: instead of using images for texture, I drew and rendered the frames of a moving creature to make it appear alive. The main idea was to create fish-like creatures with fins and wobbly eyes. I then incorporated some of my previous work on Inverse Kinematics to generate the legs. With some smoothing curve techniques, I made the shapes of the creatures smooth and visually appealing. The results are incredible visuals of creatures that move as if they were alive and following you!

kinematics.title: Inverse Kinematics
kinematics.description_short: This is a simple and fast project developed in one day. After being inspired by some YouTube videos, I decided to give it a try. The mathematics involved are simple—just angle operations. The results are quite good, though there is plenty of room for improvement.
kinematics.description_long: This is a simple and fast project developed in one day using Python, Pygame, and NumPy. After being inspired by some YouTube videos, I decided to give it a try. The mathematics involved are simple—just angle operations. The results are quite good, though there is plenty of room for improvement. The spider section was an experiment to make it work on a moving object, recreating the animation of a walking creature. The perspective is not optimal, and sometimes the legs get stuck in random positions. Nevertheless, the results are quite impressive considering the simplicity of the code.

pendulum.title: Double Pendulum
pendulum.description_short: This project was intended as a one-day coding session and ended up with me playing with the results for three days. The chaos generated by a double pendulum system is quite interesting. The math behind it is simple, involving just two (albeit large) equations. The visuals are amazing and, when properly tweaked, can mesmerize you.
pendulum.description_long: This project was intended as a one-day coding session to practice Python, Pygame, and NumPy, and ended up with me playing with the results for three days. The chaos generated by a double pendulum system is quite interesting. The math behind it is simple, involving just two (albeit large) equations. The visuals are amazing and, when properly tweaked, can mesmerize you. Simulations can be customized with a few buttons, and if you give it some time, you can modify the code to enhance it further!

boids.title: Boids Simulator
boids.description_short: Boids, or flocks, are agents that mimic the behavior of certain animals. Specifically, we can simulate the movement of birds or ants. With three simple rules—Cohesion, Alignment, and Separation—we can reproduce this fascinating behavior. Colors change based on direction, creating incredible visuals!
boids.description_long: Boids, or flocks, are agents that mimic the behavior of certain animals. Specifically, we can simulate the movement of birds or ants. With three simple rules—Cohesion, Alignment, and Separation—we can reproduce this fascinating behavior. This project is also developed with Python and Pygame, though I could not complete the NumPy version due to lack of experience. These boids are 2D, but the same approach can be used to create 3D boids that resemble swimming animals. Colors change based on direction, and textures or procedural animations (as seen in my other projects) can also be applied.

maze.title: Maze Generator Solver
maze.description_short: Mazes are an interesting application of graph and algorithm theory. They can be represented in many ways, but the objective is always to navigate from one tile to another (the exit). Here, we use pathfinding algorithms like A* or Greedy to find the best solution. Click to see how mazes are generated and solved step by step!
maze.description_long: Mazes are an interesting application of graph and algorithm theory. They can be represented in many ways, but the objective is always to navigate from one tile to another (the exit). Using Python, Pygame, and NumPy, we employ pathfinding algorithms like A* or Greedy to find the best solution. Two different maze generation algorithms are used: Origin Shift and DFS. Various strategies are then applied to solve them based on different heuristics. Many others can be implemented (also, since DFS is a somewhat simplistic maze generator), so you are more than welcome to contribute!

the_cube.title: The Cube: El Jueguito
the_cube.description_short: The Cube, also known as El Jueguito, was my first major programming project. With the aim of learning C# and Unity, I started this game as a practice project. The concept is simple: protect a cube from enemies. Round after round, more and more enemies appear, each stronger than the previous. When you can no longer hold them back, you can use the money to upgrade your weapons and survive further rounds!
the_cube.description_long: The Cube, also known as El Jueguito, was my first major programming project. With the aim of learning C# and Unity, I started this game as a practice project. Creating the visuals and assets using Photoshop resulted in a visually appealing game. The concept is simple: protect a cube from enemies. Round after round, more and more enemies appear, each stronger than the previous, and sometimes they come with a surprise. Defeating each enemy rewards you with money. When you can no longer hold them back, you can use the money to upgrade your weapons and survive further rounds!

ascii.title: Auto Image to ASCII
ascii.description_short: This project originates from the simple idea of transforming images into another format: TEXT! Using a third-party app (with proper attribution) and my UI, you can convert any video, GIF, or random image into text. Different modes are available, and you can save the outputs for later usage!
ascii.description_long: This project originates from the simple idea of transforming images into another format: TEXT! Using a third-party app (with proper attribution) and my UI, you can convert any video, GIF, or random image into text. Different modes are available, and you can save the outputs for later usage! I must admit that the way the third-party code is used might not be optimal and could potentially trigger your firewall. Nonetheless, it is fun to use and very visually appealing when you see the results.

orbits.title: Orbits Simulator
orbits.description_short: The Three-Body Problem, a good Netflix series, shows what can happen in the universe when physics are involved with large objects (planets and stars). Here, I simulate the interaction of some objects using simple Newton's equations implemented in C++. We can enable collisions and make the objects behave like bouncing balls. Super fun.
